label: sec:carbon-chains-benzene-intro
html:
We instantiate the chain–ring machinery at N = 6. The linear \mathrm{C}_6 Hopf chain assembles six carbons with a 6 \times 6 tridiagonal linking matrix. Interior carbons consume two of their four sites for the backbone. Endpoint carbons carry three dangling links each. These soft modes make linear \mathrm{C}_6 flexible.

Benzene is the closed counterpart: six carbons threaded by T(2,6), whose two components are the two delocalised \pi electrons. Its Alexander polynomial q^2 + 1 + q^{-2} replaces six pairwise Hopf weights with a single threading invariant. This explains bond-order equalisation and the \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_6 formula.

Comparing the two structures, the threaded ring binds one more atom at Alexander weight \approx 3 versus the chain's 5. The chain persists because the transition is discontinuous. The geometric reconfiguration sets an activation barrier. The estimate \Delta E \approx 2 \cdot |q + q^{-1}|_{\mathrm{mol}} \approx 193\text{--}386\,\mathrm{kJ/mol} is consistent with the experimental 200\text{--}400\,\mathrm{kJ/mol} window — an order-of-magnitude check, not a sharp parameter-free prediction: both the estimate and the window span a factor of two, and the molecular energy scale |\cdot|_{\mathrm{mol}} is an input here, not derived from the substrate calibration. The 1/2 threading factor resolves the pairwise picture's overshoot.
